subject.title: feat(cron): configurable minimum interval guardrail for recurring jobs

question: Should OpenClaw core accept `cron.minInterval` as the operator-facing recurring-job cadence guardrail, with unset/0 preserving shipped behavior and configured values rejecting or pacing fast jobs?
rationale: This PR adds a new core config surface and deliberate configured fail-closed/pacing behavior for currently valid recurring schedules, which is a product and compatibility decision beyond the mechanical patch.

options.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Fixes
options.body: Keep this core config surface, require the generated docs-map refresh, rebase, and fresh exact-head proof, then merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.

options.title: Prefer Advisory-Only Behavior
options.body: Reject enforcement for now and leave only a warning-style path for high-frequency schedules if maintainers do not want configured schedule rejection.

options.title: Defer The Config Surface
options.body: Pause this PR and keep the remaining cron guardrail work under the broader umbrella until retention, context-warning, and cadence policy are split or settled.

recommendation.title: Accept Default-Off Guardrail After Fixes
recommendation.body: Keep this core config surface, require the generated docs-map refresh, rebase, and fresh exact-head proof, then merge with the documented opt-in compatibility contract.

likelyOwner.reason: steipete is assigned on the PR and has cron-area history, making them the best available owner for the core config/product acceptance call.
